n: David asks for rescue from evil and violent people. This psalm resembles others written when David was hunted by enemies.
They plot evil in their hearts and constantly stir up conflict.
Their words are venomous — tongues sharpened like a snake’s, with viper poison behind their lips. Paul quotes this to describe human sinfulness.

f.w: adders' poison is under their lips

f.g: A musical or liturgical pause marker.

n: ‘Guard me from the wicked who plan to trip me up.’

f.g: To trip up my steps; make me fall.

n: The arrogant have hidden traps, cords, nets, and snares along his path — like a hunter setting snares for birds.

f.w: spread a net by the wayside

n: In response, David declares his loyalty: ‘You are my God; hear my pleas.’
God is the strength of his salvation, who protected his head like a helmet in battle.

f.w: thou hast covered my head in the day of battle

n: Don’t let the wicked get what they want, or they will become proud.
May the harm their own lips planned fall back on their heads.

f.w: the mischief of their own lips cover them

n: Strong images of judgment: burning coals, fire, and deep pits — echoing the fate of Sodom and the rebels of Korah’s day.
Slanderers will not last, and evil will hunt down the violent person. Evil carries its own punishment.

f.g: Literally ‘a man of tongue’ — a slanderer.

n: David knows God will defend the cause of the afflicted and secure justice for the poor.

f.w: maintain the cause of the afflicted

n: The righteous will thank God’s name, and the upright will live in his presence — the ultimate reward.

f.w: the upright shall dwell in thy presence
